Every bopomofo syllable is the corpus's own for that reading.
senses: to hit (a target); to be hit by, to fall into

hsk30l3/为.why: One sense crammed both readings: 'for (someone; something)' is wèi and 'to do; to be' is wéi, which is also the majority reading of the character in this corpus by 44 to 5.
senses: to be; to act as; to do

hsk30l3/信用卡.why: A Chinese noun is counted with a classifier and the card type has a slot for it, which 1,148 notes fill and this one did not — so a learner could recognise the word and still not say 'two of them'. Only genuinely COUNTABLE nouns are given one: most of the 3,536 noun-tagged notes without a measure word are pronouns, directions, time words and abstractions that legitimately take none.

hsk30l3/像.why: One `uc-sense` div carrying several senses joined by semicolons, under a part of speech naming several categories — so the card claimed more than it gave and nothing could be studied one sense at a time. Split into the senses the part-of-speech list already named. NOT done in bulk: 3,660 notes have a semicolon in their gloss and in most of them it separates SYNONYMS of one sense ('what kind?; what sort?'), where splitting would invent a distinction the word has not got. These 55 are the core-vocabulary notes where the parts really are different senses.

hintsWhy: AUTHORITATIVE: this map is the complete list of `not X` blocks in the Mandarin decks, including the 104 pairs the generator itself produced — it is regenerated from the finished decks, so a pair that stops colliding loses its block rather than keeping one that points at nothing. The English → Chinese card's front is the gloss and nothing else, so two notes sharing one are a question with two right answers. A group of three or more is not hinted — naming four of five answers on the front is worse than the ambiguity — and is given a distinguishing gloss in `notes` instead.

decks.whyFields: An idiom's gloss says what it MEANS and throws away what it SAYS, which is the picture that makes a four-character idiom memorable: 谢天谢地 is 'thank goodness' and it says 'thank heaven, thank earth'. The Literally line is added to the Chinese → English card, under the meaning.
